failures.criterion: scripts/dispatch/README.md's Lexeme database block, which the README now says 'is safe to run again': a rerun after an interrupted first run must recover, and must not leave the directory broken.
failures.evidence: The block exports LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$pg/server/lib" before it runs python3 to extract the tarball. On a rerun where server/ exists but data/ does not, python3's _lzma module loads the zonky liblzma.so.5 from server/lib, and the extraction then overwrites that same file in place. A first run interrupted after extraction began leaves exactly that state: a Ctrl-C (SIGINT to the run's process group, sent 0.3 s after data/ appeared) or an initdb failure, because initdb removes data/ on failure. Reproduced in this pod at da02c91: run 1 got SIGINT inside initdb and left no data/. Rerun: exit 1, 'line 13: Bus error  python3 -c ... extractall("server", filter="data")'. Every later run: exit 1, 'ImportError: .../pg/server/lib/liblzma.so.5: file too short', and the file is 0 bytes. The directory stays broken until the reader deletes $TMPDIR/pg, and the README does not say so. The export is not needed: readelf -d server/bin/postgres shows RUNPATH [$ORIGIN/../lib], and initdb with LD_LIBRARY_PATH unset exited 0. A second way to get stuck: SIGKILL inside initdb (the pod's OOM or eviction) left data/ with 5 files and no global/pg_control. The rerun skips initdb because data/ exists, then exits 1 with 'pg_ctl: error: could not open file "data/global/pg_control" for reading'. A fix: drop the LD_LIBRARY_PATH export, and make data/ appear only when complete (initdb into data.new, then mv data.new data, removing a stale data.new first). No red test: the defect is in README prose, and a source-text test is forbidden here. The steps above reproduce it.
